newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. says no evidence of Angolan military buildup.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says no evidence of Angolan military buildup.

text.p: U.N. officials in Angola said on Friday they had found no evidence of a reported military buildup of Angolan troops during a visit to the border with Zaire.

U.N. spokesman in Luanda, David Wimhurst, told Reuters U.N. force commander to Angola, Zimbabwe General Philip Sibanda, led the trip on Thursday to the Angolan northern border town of Noqui neighbouring Zaire.
"They didn't find anything unusual going on. In fact, they say everything was quite normal," Wimhurst said.
The U.N. sent 7,000 peacekeepers to Angola in 1995 to oversee the implementation of a 1994 peace agreement between the Angolan government and UNITA to end 20 years of civil war.
Noqui, which lies just south of Zaire's port of Matadi, is controlled by UNITA, an ally of Zaire's Mobutu Sese Seko government.
The Angolan government has been accused by Mobutu of backing Zaire rebels marching on the Zairean capital to topple his government.
Military analysts in Luanda say Matadi is strategically important to Kinshasa as it is the capital's only port.
Diplomats in the Angolan capital have said there had been an increase in the presence of Angolan government troops in the northern enclave of Cabinda but the reason for the buildup was not clear.
Cabinda, separated from the rest of Angola by a thin strip of Zairean territory and the Zaire river, is about 400 km (250 miles) west of Kinshasa.
Cabinda separatist guerrillas FLEC have been fighting an independence war against the Anglan government for years and hold bases in Zaire.
